title: Milking and milking techniques
competency: Describe milk, milking, hand milking and machine milking.

keywords.def: A nutrient-rich liquid food from the mammary glands of mammals.
Removing milk from the udder of cows, goats, sheep or camels.
Massaging and pulling the teats to squirt milk into a bucket.
Milking with teat cups that use vacuum and air pressure.

en.text: Milk is a nutrient-rich food from the mammary glands of mammals. Milking removes milk from the udder, by hand or by machine. Traditionally milking is done twice a day, morning and evening. Hygiene matters: wash hands, containers and teats.

screens.title: How often?
screens.ask: How many times a day is a cow traditionally milked?
screens.after: Traditionally milking happens twice a day, in the morning and evening.

screens.title: 3.2.2 Milking
paras: Milk is a nutrient-rich liquid food from the mammary glands of mammals.
It is the main food of young mammals, including babies.
Milking is removing milk from the udder of cows, goats, sheep or camels.
In local dairy farming, milking is done by hand.

screens.title: Where and when
paras: Traditionally, milking is indoors twice a day.
The cattle are tied with ropes or held in stanchions or a barn.
A barn is a farm building for livestock, equipment and fodder.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A nutrient-rich liquid food from the mammary glands of mammals.
Removing milk from the udder of cows, goats, sheep or camels.

screens.text: Milk is the primary food of:
In local dairy farming, milking is usually done by hand.
Why is milk good for people?
opts: It is nutrient-rich, with protein and calcium for growth and bones
screens.ans: It is nutrient-rich, with protein and calcium for growth and bones
screens.why: Milk is nutrient-rich. It gives protein, calcium and energy.

screens.text: Chala milks at 6 a.m. Following tradition, when is the next milking?
opts: Right after breakfast and again at noon
screens.why: Traditional milking is twice a day: morning and evening.

en.text: There are two milking methods. Hand milking massages and pulls the teats to squirt milk into a bucket; the top of the teat is pinched shut so milk is pushed out. Machine milking uses teat cups that switch between vacuum and air pressure. In both, hygiene protects the milk.

screens.title: Big farm
screens.ask: Which method can milk many cows quickly on a big farm?
screens.after: Machines milk many cows quickly. Small local farms usually milk by hand.

screens.title: 3.2.3 Milking techniques
paras: The two common methods are hand milking and machine milking.
Hand milking: massage and pull down on the teats. The milk squirts into a bucket.
table: Pinch the top of the teat, then squeeze with the other fingers
Pinch the top of the teat, then slide the fingers down

screens.title: Machine milking
paras: Teat cups are attached to the cow's teats.
The cups switch between vacuum and normal air pressure to pull out milk.
The milk is filtered and cooled, then stored in a bulk tank.

screens.title: Hygiene
paras: In both methods, protect milk from contamination.
Wash your hands, the container and the teats.
Take care that hair does not fall into the container.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Massaging and pulling the teats to squirt milk into a bucket.
Milking with teat cups that use vacuum and air pressure.

screens.text: In machine milking, what pulls the milk out?
opts: Teat cups switching between vacuum and air pressure
screens.ans: Teat cups switching between vacuum and air pressure
screens.why: The cups alternate vacuum and normal air pressure.

screens.text: Tap the hygiene steps for hand milking.
pool: Let hair fall in the bucket
screens.why: Clean hands, container and teats protect the milk.

screens.title: Machine milking in order
items: Vacuum and air pressure pull out milk
screens.why: This is the machine milking process.

screens.text: Almaz's milk spoils fast and has hairs in it. What is the most likely cause?
screens.why: Hairs and germs get in when hands, teats and containers are not clean. Hygiene protects milk from contamination.

items.text: In light of science, what are the benefits of milk for humans?
opts: Protein for growth, calcium for bones and teeth, and energy
items.ans: Protein for growth, calcium for bones and teeth, and energy
items.why: The book calls milk nutrient-rich. Its protein, calcium and energy are general science.
